title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. K is a CM field, Galois over Q, with group G. γ = {1,ρ} ≅ Z/2 ⊂ G, where ρ is complex conjugation; ρ is central because K is CM and Galois. Q̄ is the algebraic closure of Q in C. (A struck-out start, describing the set I of embeddings K→Q̄ as a G-torsor, is abandoned.)

The module and the torus. M = {φ: G→Z : φ(ρσ) = −φ(σ)}. This is the ρ-anti-invariant part of Z[G], which is isomorphic to Z[G]/(1+ρ). Grothendieck notes M ≅ Z' ⊗_{Z[γ]} Z[G], i.e. M = Ind_γ^G Z', where Z' is Z with ρ acting by −1. He also notes M ≅ M^∨ as G-modules.

By descent and duality M defines a Q-torus T. In modern terms T ≅ R_{K^+/Q}(R^1_{K/K^+} G_m), the Weil restriction of the norm-one torus of K/K^+. Equivalently, via self-duality, T ≅ R_{K/Q}G_m / R_{K^+/Q}G_m. This is the basic 'CM torus', a quotient of the Serre torus that appears in the motivic Galois group of CM motives, which is the 1965 context of the dossier.

Problem (1). Compute H^1(Q,T)' = ker(H^1(Q,T) → ∏_{p finite} H^1(Q_p,T)): the classes trivial at every finite place but not necessarily at ∞.

Tate–Nakayama gives a canonical exact sequence
0 → H^1(Q,T)' → Ĥ_0(G, Y_∞ ⊗ M^∨) → Ĥ_0(G, M^∨) → 0.
- Y_∞ is the free abelian group on the archimedean places of K, i.e. Z[G/γ].
- The second map comes from the augmentation Y_∞ → Z.
- The middle term is ⊕_{v|∞} H^1(R,T); the right term is the global obstruction term (Ĥ^{-1} of the dual).

By Shapiro's lemma for M = Ind_γ^G Z', the sequence becomes
0 → H^1(Q,T)' → Ĥ_0(γ, Y_∞⊗Z') → Ĥ_0(γ, Z') → 0,
that is, Y_∞ ⊗ Z/2 → Z/2, the sum of coefficients.

Conclusion: H^1(Q,T)' ≅ the F_2-linear combinations of the archimedean places of K with coefficient sum zero. It is an F_2-vector space of dimension [K^+:Q] − 1.

Classical check:
- Shapiro gives H^1(Q,T) = H^1(K^+, R^1_{K/K^+}G_m) = K^{+×}/N K^×.
- Classes trivial at all finite places are elements that are local norms at every finite place, modulo global norms.
- By the Hasse norm theorem (K/K^+ is cyclic) such a class is determined by its signs at the real places of K^+. Each real place is ramified in K, so local norms there are the positive reals.
- The product formula for the quadratic Hilbert symbol forces the number of negative signs to be even, and every even pattern occurs.
- Real places of K^+ correspond bijectively to archimedean places of K, giving the same answer.

The next page is unrelated (effective and strict epimorphic families in a category); the previous page is an earlier draft of this one.
errors: In the γ-reduced sequence Grothendieck writes Ĥ_0(γ, Y_∞) where it should be Ĥ_0(γ, Y_∞ ⊗ Z'). Because ρ acts trivially on G/γ (ρ central), both give Y_∞/2, so the final answer is unaffected.
Notation wavers between H^1 and Ĥ^1 for the Galois cohomology of T. This is harmless.

ideas.what: The CM torus with character group Ind_γ^G Z' (anti-invariant functions on G), i.e. R_{K^+/Q} R^1_{K/K^+} G_m, as a piece of the motivic Galois group of CM motives
ideas.modern_name: CM torus / quotient of the Serre torus S^K
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (Abelian l-adic representations, 1968); Deligne, Milne, Langlands (Taniyama group, 1979–82)

ideas.what: Exact sequence computing the classes in H^1(Q,T) trivial at all finite places via Ĥ_0(G, Y_∞⊗X) → Ĥ_0(G, X)
ideas.modern_name: Tate–Nakayama / Poitou–Tate description of ker^1 relative to the finite places (Kottwitz-style)

ideas.what: Result: the group is the F_2-span of the archimedean places of K with zero coefficient sum (dimension [K^+:Q] − 1)
ideas.modern_name: Consequence of the Hasse norm theorem plus the Hilbert reciprocity law

missed.claim: Early (dossier dated 1965) evidence that Grothendieck was computing arithmetic invariants (local–global behaviour at real places) of the CM torus underlying the motivic Galois group of CM motives. This predates the Serre/Deligne/Langlands treatment of the Serre torus and the Taniyama group. The computation itself is classical.
missed.quote: C'est un G-module, qui définit par descente et dualité un tore T sur Q ... H^1(Q,T)' ≃ groupe des combinaisons linéaires à coeff dans F_2 des places à l'infini de K, à somme des coefficients nulle.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents the motivic-Galois-theoretic origin of questions about real points and gerbes for CM motives, later treated by Deligne, Milne and Langlands–Rapoport. There is no new mathematics here.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a correct but standard Tate–Nakayama / Hasse norm theorem computation. The only interest is historical: Grothendieck working concretely with the CM (Serre-type) torus in the 1965 motivic Galois context.

The first exact sequence begins '0 → Ĥ^1(Q,T)'' (hat present), with arrows labeled α and β.
